prompt: Your real-time customer chat agent is suffering from unacceptable 12-second response latency. Most queries are simple FAQ lookups or greeting intents. Which architectural pattern immediately mitigates this bottleneck?

options.text: Model routing: use a small, fast model for greetings/FAQ and route only complex reasoning queries to the large frontier LLM.
Add 5 more intermediate reasoning steps to the large model's prompt.
Disable all caching layers to ensure fresh generation every turn.
Switch from asynchronous tool execution to sequential blocking calls.

explanation: Judicious model selection and routing dispatches routine tasks to small, fast models (sub-150ms), reserving large LLMs for complex planning, which drastically reduces average user latency and cloud inference costs.

prompt: Match each production challenge to its primary architectural mitigation strategy:

pairs.left: LLM hallucinations in legal or financial answers
Transient 504 timeouts on third-party external tool APIs
pairs.right: Automatic retries with exponential backoff & fallbacks

pairs.left: Human reviewer burnout from approving 5,000 queries daily
pairs.right: Strategic touchpoints: gate only high-stakes threshold actions

explanation: RAG anchors outputs in source truth; exponential retries absorb transient network glitches; selective touchpoints eliminate reviewer fatigue; and input guardrails neutralize adversarial prompt overrides.

prompt: An engineering team builds a multi-agent system where Agent A calls Agent B, which calls Agent C synchronously without timeouts, circuit breakers, or error try/catch blocks. What catastrophic production failure will inevitably occur?

options.text: Cascading failure and system deadlock: if Agent C hangs or times out, the entire multi-agent pipeline freezes indefinitely and crashes all waiting user sessions.
The language model will automatically write the missing code at runtime.
The database will increase its read throughput automatically.

explanation: Without error boundaries, timeouts, and graceful degradation, any single component failure in a synchronous chain cascades upward, leading to system-wide deadlocks, memory exhaustion, and total outage.
